evals.query: I have a Kora 2.0 Java service. Cache OrderDto lookups by their UUID id in an in-process cache.
expected_behavior: Adds io.koraframework:cache-caffeine and annotationProcessor "io.koraframework:annotation-processors", versioned through the io.koraframework:kora-bom platform
Extends CaffeineCacheModule from io.koraframework.cache.caffeine on the @KoraApp interface
Declares a typed @Cache("orders.cache") interface extending CaffeineCache<UUID, OrderDto>, importing io.koraframework.cache.annotation.Cache
Annotates the read method with @Cacheable(OrderCache.class) so the single UUID parameter becomes the key, and keeps the enclosing class non-final
Adds an application.conf section at the @Cache path with maximumSize and/or expireAfterWrite
Does not add the generated $OrderCache_Module to the @KoraApp extends clause
Does not use ru.tinkoff.kora imports, the kora-parent BOM, @EnableCaching, or any Spring/Micronaut caching annotation

evals.query: Kotlin Kora 2.0 service: add an in-process cache for getOrder(id: UUID).
expected_behavior: Adds io.koraframework:cache-caffeine and ksp("io.koraframework:symbol-processors") through the kora-bom platform
Declares @Cache("orders.cache") interface OrderCache : CaffeineCache<UUID, OrderDto>
Marks the service class open AND the annotated function open, and says why (the KSP aspect refuses a non-open target)
Uses @Cacheable(OrderCache::class) with the Kotlin class-literal syntax
Does not use suspend on the cached function, and does not claim suspend or Flow is supported by cache AOP in Kora 2.0

evals.query: Porting this method from Kora 1.x: @CachePut(value = OrderCache.class, parameters = { "id" }) public OrderDto update(UUID id, OrderRequest request). It no longer compiles under Kora 2.0.
expected_behavior: Identifies that the attribute was renamed and writes @CachePut(value = OrderCache.class, args = { "id" }) (or args = "id")
States that @Cacheable, @CachePut and @CacheInvalidate each expose exactly value(), args() and mode() in Kora 2.0 — there is no parameters attribute
Explains that an empty/absent args means every method parameter forms the key, which is why update methods must name the key parameter explicitly
In Kotlin writes args = ["id"] as an array literal
Does not suggest a project-wide search and replace of 'parameters =' (HOCON/YAML keys named parameters would be corrupted)

evals.query: My Kora 1.x code has @CacheInvalidate(value = OrderCache.class, invalidateAll = true) on a purge() method. What is the Kora 2.0 equivalent?
expected_behavior: Replaces it with @CacheInvalidateAll(OrderCache.class) from io.koraframework.cache.annotation
States that the invalidateAll attribute no longer exists on @CacheInvalidate — its attributes are value, args and mode
Mentions that @CacheInvalidateAll is repeatable (container @CacheInvalidateAlls) so it can be stacked across cache levels
Warns that @CacheInvalidate and @CacheInvalidateAll may not be combined on the same method
For a Redis cache, warns that invalidateAll with a blank keyPrefix issues FLUSHALL against the whole Redis instance
Does not keep invalidateAll = true or invent an invalidateAll() attribute elsewhere

evals.query: Set up a distributed Redis-backed cache for OrderDto in Kora 2.0 so several pods share the cached state.
expected_behavior: Adds io.koraframework:cache-redis-lettuce — not cache-redis, which does not exist in the Kora 2.0 BOM

Extends LettuceRedisCacheModule from io.koraframework.cache.redis.lettuce on @KoraApp, and states that RedisCacheModule alone supplies no RedisCacheClient (graph fails with 'No component found for dependency: io.koraframework.cache.redis.RedisCacheClient')
Declares @Cache("orders.cache") interface OrderCache extends RedisCache<UUID, @Json OrderDto> with @Json on the value type argument, and annotates OrderDto itself @Json
Configures a lettuce { uri = ... } section with the URI and credentials externalized through environment substitution

Sets a non-blank keyPrefix in the per-cache section and explains that it is required — a missing value fails graph init with ConfigValueException: Config expected value, but got null at path: 'ROOT.orders.cache.keyPrefix'
Does not use RedisTemplate, a hand-rolled Jedis/Lettuce client, or ru.tinkoff.kora imports

evals.query: Kotlin Kora 2.0: my app extends RedisCacheModule and the build fails with "No component found for dependency: io.koraframework.cache.redis.RedisCacheClient (no tags)". Why?
expected_behavior: Explains that RedisCacheModule lives in cache-redis-common and is transport-neutral: it supplies telemetry and the key/value mappers but no RedisCacheClient
Switches the dependency to io.koraframework:cache-redis-lettuce and the @KoraApp interface to LettuceRedisCacheModule
Notes that LettuceRedisCacheModule extends both RedisCacheModule and LettuceModule, so nothing else needs adding
Reminds that the lettuce { uri = ... } section is required and that uri has no default
Does not suggest declaring a RedisCacheClient @Component by hand

evals.query: My Kora 2.0 cached method takes an OrderContext(tenantId, orderId, traceId) but the cache key is only tenantId+orderId. Compilation fails with "No component found for dependency: com.example.OrderService.OrderContextMapping (no tags)".
expected_behavior: Implements io.koraframework.cache.CacheKeyMapper<OrderCache.Key, OrderContext> and applies it with @Mapping(OrderContextMapping.class) from io.koraframework.common.annotation

Adds @Component to the mapper class and states that this is required even for a nested class and even when the mapper has no constructor dependencies, because the cache processor always injects the mapper into the generated AOP proxy
Contrasts this with HTTP mappers, where a dependency-free @Component mapper instead causes 'Multiple components match dependency'
Uses CacheKeyMapper.CacheKeyMapper2 (a nested interface) when the key is derived from two separate method parameters instead of one object
Does not use jakarta.annotation.Nonnull on the mapper (Kora 2.0 modules are JSpecify @NullMarked)
Does not invent SpEL key expressions or a keyGenerator attribute

evals.query: I need to cache by tenantId plus orderId in a Kora 2.0 Caffeine cache. How do I model the composite key?
expected_behavior: Declares a nested record (Java) or data class (Kotlin) Key(tenantId, orderId) inside the @Cache interface and extends CaffeineCache<OrderCache.Key, OrderDto>
Explains that the processor emits new Key(tenantId, orderId) because the key type has a public constructor matching the selected parameters in order, so no mapper is needed
Uses args to reorder or subset when the method signature does not match the constructor order
Notes that with no matching constructor the processor instead requires a CacheKeyMapper.CacheKeyMapperN component
Does not invent a condition or unless attribute on the cache annotations

evals.query: Kora 2.0: I want a fast local Caffeine L1 in front of a shared Redis L2 for UserResponse. Wire it up.
expected_behavior: Extends both CaffeineCacheModule and LettuceRedisCacheModule on @KoraApp, with cache-caffeine and cache-redis-lettuce dependencies
Declares two @Cache interfaces with distinct config paths — one extending CaffeineCache, the other RedisCache<..., @Json ...> — and notes that a single interface may not extend both contracts
Stacks @Cacheable with the Caffeine annotation first and the Redis annotation second, explaining that the caches are consulted in annotation order and that an L2 hit back-fills L1
Repeats @CachePut / @CacheInvalidate for both levels with identical args, noting that differing args lists are a compile error
Gives L1 a shorter expireAfterWrite than L2 and keeps a non-blank keyPrefix on the Redis level
Does not use a @Caching meta-annotation, field injection, or a single interface extending both cache contracts

evals.query: I enabled the metrics module in my Kora 2.0 service but no cache metrics show up in Prometheus. The cache itself works.
expected_behavior: Explains that Kora 2.0 cache telemetry defaults are logging.enabled = false and metrics.enabled = false, while tracing.enabled = true
Adds telemetry.metrics.enabled = true inside that cache's own config section (per cache, not globally)

For a Caffeine cache notes that the metrics come from Micrometer's CaffeineCacheMetrics binder registered by CaffeineFactory over a recordStats() cache (cache.gets, cache.puts, cache.evictions, cache.eviction.weight, cache.size), and only when a MeterRegistry is present
For a Redis cache names the Kora series cache.operation.duration and cache.requests (hit/miss in cache.result) with their system.config / cache.operation / cache.origin tags
Does not claim metrics are on by default or invent a recordStats config key
Does not suggest a MeterFilter or disabling Caffeine metrics to avoid a duplicate cache.gets meter registration

evals.query: Kotlin Kora 2.0 build fails: "AOP aspect cannot be applied to class 'com.example.OrderService' because the class is not open." I only added @Cacheable.
expected_behavior: Explains that Kora cache aspects are compile-time subclass proxies, so in Kotlin the class must be open
Also marks the annotated function open, and quotes the companion error 'AOP aspect cannot be applied to function ... because the function is not open.'
States that in Kora 2.0 this is a hard compile error, not a silently skipped aspect
Gives the Java equivalent: the class must not be final ('AOP aspect cannot be applied to class ... because the class is final.') and the method must be neither final nor private
Mentions self-invocation: a call from inside the same class bypasses the generated $OrderService__AopProxy
Does not suggest AspectJ, runtime proxies, all-open compiler plugins, or @EnableCaching

evals.query: In Kora 2.0 I do not want the Redis write on my request thread when updating an order. Is there anything built in?
expected_behavior: Points at mode = CacheMode.ASYNC on @CachePut / @CacheInvalidate / @CacheInvalidateAll / @Cacheable (io.koraframework.cache.annotation.CacheMode, values SYNC and ASYNC, default SYNC)
Explains that only the write side moves off-thread: the lookup performed by @Cacheable is always synchronous

States that the work is handed to an Executor requested as @Tag(CacheMode.class), supplied as a @DefaultComponent by CacheCommonModule, which starts a virtual thread named kora-cache-N per operation and only logs failures
Warns that ASYNC on a Caffeine cache is ignored with the compile warning 'Cache async mode is ignored for CaffeineCache ...'
Mentions that the executor can be replaced with a @Component @Tag(CacheMode.class) Executor
Does not suggest returning CompletionStage or making the method suspend — cache AOP in 2.0 rejects both

evals.query: My Kora 2.0 service dies at startup with ConfigValueException: Config expected value, but got null at path: 'ROOT.orders.cache.keyPrefix'. The section exists.
expected_behavior: Identifies RedisCacheConfig.keyPrefix() as a required config value — no default and not @Nullable — and adds it to that cache's section
Clarifies that this fails at graph initialization, not at compile time, because the generated cache module resolves the config with mapOrThrow
Explains that the effective Redis key is keyPrefix + ':' + mapped key, so the separator must not be added by hand

Warns that setting keyPrefix = "" is accepted but makes invalidateAll() fall back to FLUSHALL, and notes that the empty-prefix warning is emitted through a no-op logger unless that cache section sets telemetry.logging.enabled = true, so by default the wipe is silent
Recommends a distinct prefix per cache to avoid key collisions in a shared Redis database

evals.query: In Kora 2.0 I need manual get-or-load on a cache without @Cacheable, because the key is generated inside the method. What are my options?
expected_behavior: Injects the typed @Cache interface as a normal component and uses the Cache<K, V> API: get, put, computeIfAbsent, invalidate, invalidateAll plus the bulk overloads
Notes that get returns null on a miss and that put silently ignores null keys and null values rather than throwing
Offers LoadableCache built with asLoadableSimple(loader) for a single-key loader or asLoadable(bulkLoader) for a Collection -> Map loader, exposed from a @Module method
Does not claim the Cache contract has contains, containsValue, asMap or size
Does not use a CacheManager abstraction, and does not claim @Cacheable can key on a value computed inside the method body

evals.query: Migrating a Kora 1.x service to 2.0: @Cacheable on a method returning Mono<OrderDto>, and another on a suspend fun. Both now fail to compile.
expected_behavior: States that Kora 2.0 contracts are synchronous on virtual threads and cache AOP supports only synchronous returns — Publisher/Mono/Flux, CompletionStage/CompletableFuture and Kotlin suspend are all rejected
Rewrites the methods to return the plain value (or Optional<T> in Java, T? in Kotlin)
Quotes the diagnostic shape: '@Cacheable cannot be applied to ... because return type ... is not supported by the Java cache AOP aspect'
Notes that @Cacheable and @CachePut also reject void/Unit, while @CacheInvalidate and @CacheInvalidateAll allow it
Mentions Cache<K, Optional<T>> as the way to memoize a negative lookup
Does not add reactor-core or kotlinx-coroutines to make the old signature work

evals.query: Kora 2.0 with a Redis cache: my @Cacheable method throws when the upstream service is down. Will the cache swallow that exception like it swallows Redis errors, and will anything be cached?
expected_behavior: Distinguishes Redis backend failures, which AbstractRedisCache records in telemetry and swallows (a failed read is treated as a miss), from exceptions thrown by the loader
States that an exception from the @Cacheable method body (the computeIfAbsent mapping function) is recorded in telemetry and propagates to the caller
States that nothing is written to Redis for that key when the loader throws
anti_behavior: Claims the Redis cache swallows the method's own exception and returns null
Recommends catching the exception inside the method and returning null so the cache stays quiet
